# Draft:Ram Baboo Tiwari

Ram Baboo Tiwari is an Indian water conservationist and social activist from Andhav village in Banda district of the Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh. He is known for his work in restoring traditional water bodies and for community-based water conservation efforts in drought-prone areas.
Early life and background
Tiwari was born in Andhav, a village in Banda district of Uttar Pradesh, a region frequently affected by water scarcity and drought conditions. His early experiences with water shortages influenced his later involvement in water conservation initiatives.
Work
Tiwari has been actively involved in the restoration and rejuvenation of ponds across the Bundelkhand region, with the aim of improving groundwater levels and water availability. He continues to be engaged in water conservation initiatives in the region.
He is the founder of the Mangal Bhoomi Foundation, a voluntary organization based in Banda that works on water conservation and rural development.
He has promoted a water conservation campaign under the slogan "Khet ka paani khet mein, gaon ka paani gaon mein", encouraging rainwater harvesting and local water retention.
Recognition
Tiwari has been referred to as the “Jal Purush” (Water Man) of Bundelkhand for his contributions to water conservation.
His work was mentioned by the Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi, in the radio programme Mann Ki Baat on 27 June 2021.In September 2020, he was awarded the Water Heroes Award by the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India.
He has also received the Jal Prahari Award for his contributions to water conservation.
Publications
In 2021, Tiwari edited the book Neer Gatha: Jal Sankat – Samasya, Samadhan evam Sambhavnayein, which discusses water crisis, its challenges, and possible solutions.
